cards.reason: Version context only (v0 legacy, v1 separate); it corrects the prior claim's picture of BAML but changes nothing in the harness.
The hard/recorded split is the same change as T-08: hard checks throw, soft checks are recorded on the object for the judge.

cards.trial_measurement: In the B-13 trial, record each case as pass/fail/needs-owner/not-run. Yes if at least one run would have read green under plain pass/fail when zero cases ran or some were infra-skipped.
cards.reason: A four-state result where zero cases run is never green fits the honest-empty rule. It only matters once a brief-test runner exists.
Useful correction: BAML tests call live models, so 'no API calls' means prompt preview only. The render-check idea it points to is R-09.
The optimizer needs a scored test corpus we lack, plus an install and API keys. Premature.

cards.trial_measurement: In the B-13 trial, count cases whose tool_status is not web_ok or whose agent call errored, and exclude them from the pass rate. Yes (make it a standing rule) if excluding them changes any brief's verdict.
cards.reason: Vendor-admitted failure mode. Separating infrastructure outcomes from content outcomes is a mandatory rule for any brief scoring.
Same change as T-08 (per-card script checks recorded, not rejected). Cross-field if/then rules wait until someone confirms the validator supports them.
Validate-and-retry is already the design. The card itself says not to import leniency; at most a one-line note in the design doc that strictness is deliberate.
Vendor benchmark with no stated method, on 2024 models. Not evidence.

cards.trial_measurement: Take accepted payloads from the journals of this sweep and one earlier run and replay them through the T-08 checks with no model call. Yes if the checks flag at least one real defect the judge missed, or catch a deliberately injected contract regression.
cards.reason: Parse-as-a-pure-function becomes offline replay of saved StructuredOutput objects. It needs a fixture home, because scripts have no filesystem.

cards.trial_measurement: First establish whether agent() or the journal exposes StructuredOutput rejection counts. If it does, log retries per brief over 3 runs. Yes if any brief exceeds a 10% retry rate (a brief defect signal); if counts are not exposed, drop it.
cards.reason: The cheapest brief-quality metric, if the count is observable. The baseline says it is not measured today.
Corrects the idea that BAML retries on schema mismatch: it retries only on transport errors. Nothing to take.

Define each §5 verdict and severity value once, in a shared schema constant, and have briefs reference it rather than restate it. Removes drift between briefs. A JSON Schema enum has no per-value description, so use oneOf with const and description, or one description string.
Directive text was observed in fetched pages during this run. Add a research-contract rule and field so a reader reports directive text found in a source rather than acting on it.
Settles adoption: BAML is codegen plus a CLI with its own API keys, and cannot be imported into a Workflow script.
Amends the prior claim: 'typed prompt functions' describes the legacy v0, and v1 is a pre-1.0 language. Not an install candidate.
Measured repo facts: active, Apache-2.0, v1 nightlies, v0 slowing. Context for the owner only.
BAML injects the schema into the prompt and repairs the reply, the opposite of our tool-layer reject-and-retry. A useful contrast, with no change.
Vendor benchmark on 2024 models, with a results table that did not render.

Add a §5 rule: any script step that filters, de-duplicates or normalises a returned array reports received and kept counts plus a reason per drop. The silent-drop pattern recurs across several issue reports.
Same change as T-08: name schema-enforced rules and code-computed checks as two classes; the computed checks travel to the judge.

cards.trial_measurement: Same as D-11: check whether retry counts are observable, then compare per-brief retry rates against a 10% threshold.
cards.reason: Same idea as D-11 (a schema-attempt budget visible to the caller), and it depends on what agent() exposes.
Same change as D-13: every property and enum member gets a one-line meaning. The token-saving claim is irrelevant here.
A pure in-script brief lint before any agent() call: CONTEXT block present verbatim, no tier word, required ⊆ properties, enums non-empty. Zero model cost; it catches hand-edit regressions.
A dry-run flag makes a script return its assembled prompts and schemas instead of calling agent(), so a brief edit reviews as a text diff before any spend. Script-only.
The optimizer is premature. Its useful limit (separate infra failures from content failures) is D-06.
Proposed for the KS design: a `ks guide` printed from the same command definitions, plus a test that every subcommand appears in it. No model, and it prevents doc drift.
The examples are app-side extraction. Area (d) only, and FixFlow has no LLM features planned.
Settles it: BAML clients are raw API calls and cannot drive Claude Code subagents with tools, so BAML cannot stand in for agent().
Telemetry and trace-header risks are install-cost context for the owner. Nothing to adopt.
Vendor-run, 2024 models. Script-side coercion would weaken the deliberate strictness, and no retry cost has been shown.
Marketing. Its one lesson (assertions that cannot be satisfied) is carried by T-03.
Notes fields, tool_status and UNVERIFIABLE already give the escape hatch. The evidence was disputed (B-04).
Same change as I-01: evidence and explanation properties come before verdict and severity.
We do not control how the tool renders the schema. The token saving does not apply.
Scripts compute counts from array lengths; never ask an agent for a count. The numeric-confidence part is the T-01 trial.
A single self-reported project that mostly confirms the existing human-gated design.
Measured, small n: give agents short handles and map back in code; never make an agent echo full SHAs or UUIDs. Same rule as T-10 for verifier inputs.

cards.trial_measurement: Add 'list the dimensions of the change and the combinations the tests cover' to the next 3 Opus review briefs. Yes if at least one confirmed defect comes from an uncovered combination.
cards.reason: A single post-mortem. Cheap to add to review briefs, but unproven here.
Same change as T-08: deterministic JS checks over the returned object, hard versus recorded.
Pre-1.0 language whose syntax breaks almost every release. Strengthens 'do not install'.

cards.trial_measurement: In the B-13 trial, check whether each journal entry can be tied to a brief version without manual work. If not, add a brief_sha field per agent call; yes if the comparison then needs no hand matching.
cards.reason: Recording by default helps diff brief versions. The journal already keeps outputs; only the brief version is missing.

cards.trial_measurement: At the next hand-edit of one brief, take 10–30 past inputs and run the old and new brief 3× each. Score with T-08 checks and a verdict-field diff, include one must-fail case, and exclude infra-failed cases. Count disagreements and owner review minutes. Yes if the new brief is no worse on checks and the owner reviews only the disagreements, at an agent cost the owner accepts.
cards.reason: Closest fit to area (b): a relative gate, repeats, and review of disagreements only. Buildable as a Workflow script with no BAML.
Confirms existing rules. Its golden-set naming is carried by B-13 and T-02.
Classifier endpoints cannot be called from Claude Code. Mirrors enums we already have.

cards.trial_measurement: Audit the 'likelihood 0–1' values across the last 3 runs' journals. Yes (replace with a defined enum) if more than 80% fall on 3 or fewer distinct values, or if they show no relation to the skeptic's outcome.
cards.reason: §5 still carries a model-asserted number (likelihood). A rubric enum may carry the same signal more honestly.

cards.trial_measurement: Same as D-10: replay saved accepted objects, diffing verdict and severity fields only.
cards.reason: Every validated stage output is already a probe, so a golden set comes almost free. Same trial as D-10.

cards.trial_measurement: Built into the B-13 trial: one must-fail case that must fail, 'cannot judge' when an input is missing, and 3 repeats. Yes if the must-fail case fails and repeats change at least one verdict compared with a single run.
cards.reason: Safeguards for the eval itself, measured on the author's own run. These are the design rules of the B-13 trial.

cards.trial_measurement: A one-off: replay one research lane's brief on Sonnet and on Opus and diff the cards. The owner hand-labels disagreements only. Yes (the routing holds) if Sonnet's disagreements are mostly no worse.
cards.reason: Tests the tier split cheaply. A one-off check, not a standing gate.
Fixed §5 contracts are already the 'freeze the shape, edit the prose' discipline.

cards.trial_measurement: Give one Opus pass this sweep's six lane transcripts or journals and ask it to list wasted calls and ignored brief rules; the owner or Fable triages. Yes if at least 3 confirmed, actionable brief edits come out of one pass.
cards.reason: Improves briefs without writing tests. It depends on whether transcripts, not just return values, are reachable.

cards.trial_measurement: Same task, two CONTEXT variants (current and trimmed), 3 runs each. Compare tool calls, tokens and T-08 check pass rate. Yes (trim) if the trimmed variant is no worse on checks and at least 15% cheaper.
cards.reason: The length of the CONTEXT block is untested. The cited win relied on a tool we do not have, so expect weaker transfer.

Lead card: deterministic JS checks on each returned object (quote ≤15 words, evidence pattern, unique ids, each could_not_read in urls_attempted), then one bounded retry that names the failed check. Free, and it lands directly in scripts.
Audit §5 for required fields with no 'unknown' path (source_date, quote on a summarised card), since those invite invention. A one-pass schema review.
Number the evidence handed to verifiers and skeptics; they cite ids, and the script rejects unknown ids, so no fabricated URL can enter a verification step.
Investor-hosted claims about SAP. It solves malformed text, which forced tool output already prevents.
A separate product (Jev); product area (d) only, with no LLM features planned.
CLAUDE.md invariants plus import-linter and ESLint already do this.
The owner critique rounds are already the read gate. No change proposed.

cards.trial_measurement: Only as a parameter of the B-13 trial: start with about 30 cases drawn from past accepted runs. Yes if the disagreement rate is stable between the first and second 15 cases.
cards.reason: A rule of thumb with no data; usable only as a sizing default.

Lead for field order: in every §5 contract, explanation/basis and evidence properties come before verdict and severity, and all are required (I-14). The effect is contested on 2024 models but the rule costs nothing.

cards.trial_measurement: A B-13 rule: identical prompts across variants and a deterministic scorer. Yes if two scorers do not swing the result more than the treatment does.
cards.reason: The choice of scorer alone moved results more than the treatment. A design rule for comparing brief versions.

cards.trial_measurement: As I-02: before any change to how a brief shapes output, run an A/B per model with a deterministic scorer.
cards.reason: The effect depends on model and task, so test, do not assume. Folds into the B-13 trial.
Same change as I-01; independent practitioner reports of the field-order effect.
UNVERIFIABLE, tool_status and honest-empty already put the escape hatch in the schema. Gaps are covered by the T-09 audit.
The independent check found no replication of the vendor BFCL headline. Do not cite it.
Our contracts already use the plain schema subset. Measured on open models only.
'path:line — quote' evidence and 15-word quotes already keep bulky text out of JSON. Measured on 2024 models with a code task.

cards.trial_measurement: Treat any §5 key rename or description change as a trigger for the B-13 regression run. Yes if a rename shows a check-pass-rate shift beyond run-to-run variance.
cards.reason: Field names are prompt text, so a contract rename is an untested behaviour change today.

cards.trial_measurement: Same as I-09; confirm effect sizes in the full paper first.
cards.reason: A 2026 peer-reviewed reinforcement of I-09, but only the abstract was read.
A valid schema is not a correct value. The design already rests on evidence strings and fresh-context skeptics.
The harness runs schema agents on Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1, which reject a provider-forced tool_choice, so enforcement must already be tool-layer validation.

First-party docs: rename schema fields like 'reasoning' or 'rationale' to 'explanation' or 'basis' to avoid reasoning_extraction refusals, and list a refusal as a known failure state. A grep and a rename.
Part of the I-01 change: make ordered fields required, and keep enum values distinct by more than case. Tool-layer validation would reject case drift anyway.
Adopting BAML now means adopting a language and runtime. Supports 'ideas, not tool'.
Forced tool output is mainstream, and the harness already uses it.
Lenient parsing is irrelevant where scripts never parse text. Strict rejection stays the honest default.
Vendor benchmark, obsolete models; the tool-call layer already solves the problem SAP addresses.
Correction: BAML's comparison pages are v0 claims, so do not cite them for the current product.
Add to the R-09 brief lint: no raw JSON Schema pasted into brief prose; the forced tool already carries it. A third-party measurement found schema-echo failures.
Token-level constraint libraries need logits that hosted Claude does not expose. Out of scope.
Same paper as I-07. Our contracts already keep to the simple subset.
A design-doc rule: a schema failure is retried at the same tier and never silently escalated; only infrastructure failures may change tier, by orchestrator decision.

cards.trial_measurement: Using the R-10 dry-run flag, swap agent() for an inline stub returning canned objects in one gate script, then inject a REFUTED and an UNVERIFIABLE verdict. Yes if this finds a routing bug, or confirms routing, faster than a live run.
cards.reason: An offline layer-1 test of script control flow. It can live inside the script, with no imports.
Same change as T-08: deterministic assertions over structured output with no framework.

cards.trial_measurement: Same as D-06.
cards.reason: No optimizer. Its only transferable rule (infra failures are not content failures) is D-06.
Briefs live in git and runs cite commit SHAs.
Applies only to prose restatements of a schema, which P-05 says to remove anyway.

cards.trial_measurement: Same as D-11: whether the rejection count is observable, and the per-brief rate if it is.
cards.reason: The validator's specific error text is the repair signal; the retry count as a brief signal is D-11.

prior_claim.reasoning: The cards confirm the claim, with one amendment. Why not the tool: BAML generates a host-language client that calls provider APIs and cannot be imported into a no-import Workflow script (D-15). Its clients are raw completions, so they cannot drive Claude Code subagents with tools, and the request for a Claude Code client is still an open issue (R-14). It puts the schema in the prompt and repairs the reply, the opposite of our tool-layer reject-and-retry (R-03). Its tests call live models and need API keys; 'no API calls' means prompt preview only (D-04, P-11). Its benchmarks are vendor-run on 2024 models with no independent replication (I-06). Install cost: v0 is legacy, and v1 is a pre-1.0 language that breaks syntax nearly every release (R-01, B-11, I-15), with open telemetry and trace-header issues (R-15). Amendment: 'BAML is for application code' describes v0 only, and its test value is ideas, not free tests. Every adopt or trial card (T-08, I-01, I-13, R-05, R-09, B-13, D-11) is plain JS in a script, a schema edit, or a design rule.
prior_claim.where_tool_would_earn_install: None found in the harness or the knowledge store. The only conceivable landing is area (d): a future FixFlow LLM feature such as typed extraction from customer messages, and none is planned.
prior_claim.what_would_prove_it: For the harness: BAML ships a client type that runs Claude Code subagents with tools, and a pinned baml-cli test run over 30 brief cases catches regressions the B-13 plain-script trial misses, at no higher cost. For the product (only if the owner approves an LLM feature): on 50–100 real customer messages, pinned BAML v1 beats the plain Anthropic SDK with strict tool output on value accuracy by more than run-to-run variance, with no telemetry egress.

notes: I scored from the cards as given and fetched no sources; the design doc is not in this worktree, so baseline facts come from the task text. Duplicate cards share their lead card's disposition: T-08 covers D-02, D-07, R-06, B-10 and P-11; I-01 covers B-04, I-04 and I-14; D-13 covers R-08; B-08 covers T-10. I-12 is marked already-done on an inference: the harness runs schema agents on models that reject a provider-forced tool_choice. T-03, I-02, I-03, D-06 and T-15 are design rules folded into the B-13 trial, not separate trials. Smaller adopts not in the top five: D-13, D-14, B-06, B-08/T-10, T-09, R-10, P-05, P-09 and R-12 (the last is a proposal for the KS design). The D-11 and P-15 trials should start by checking whether agent() exposes schema-retry counts; if it does not, drop them. One §5 contract change flagged for trial is T-01: likelihood is a number the model asserts, the kind of value B-06 and T-01 warn against.
